description:
After bd:JMAP-510h.1 landed, handle_filenode_copy supports onExists=replace and onDestroyRemoveChildren=true. When the destination has a colliding node, the handler now destroys it (and cascades to descendants when the flag is true). The destructions are real and observable via Foo/changes — but RFC 8620 §5.4 does not define a 'destroyed' field on the Foo/copy response, so the client has no in-response signal for what the copy destroyed.

Workspace decision needed:
(a) Accept the gap: clients learn about the destruction via Foo/changes between snapshots. RFC-faithful, minimal surface area.
(b) Extend the response shape with a non-standard 'destroyed' / 'destroyedIds' field on FileNode/copy. Better client UX but introduces a non-RFC-defined field.
(c) File the gap upstream against draft-ietf-jmap-filenode-13 (a 'with the same behaviour' that destroys nodes ought to make those destructions visible to the client without an extra method round-trip).

Code today follows option (a): handler tracks the destroys internally (mutates state, sets the mutated flag for newState calculation) but does NOT surface them. See note at handle_filenode_copy around 'destroyed_list' in src/filenode.rs.

Suggested first step: file as a draft errata / discussion item with the FileNode draft authors. If accepted, option (b) becomes the right path; otherwise document the limitation in PLAN.md and the README.
title: FileNode/copy onExists=replace silently destroys nodes with no wire signal
